newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB asset management firms set merger terms.
newsitem.headline: DKB asset management firms set merger terms.

text.p: Three investment management firms in the Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) group said on Wednesday that they had decided on the terms for their merger.

Asahi Investment Trust Management Co, Kankaku Capital Management Co and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Investment Management Co said in a joint statement they would merge on October 1, with Asahi Investment absorbing the other two firms and changing its name to Dai-Ichi Kangyo Asahi Asset Management Co Ltd.
The merged entity will be capitalised at 2.05 billion yen.
Dai-Ichi Kangyo Investment Management is an affiliate of DKB, while the other two are affiliates of Kankaku Securities Co Ltd, which is part of the DKB group.

Each share of Kankaku Capital Management, with a face value of 50,000 yen, will be exchanged for six shares of Asahi Investment, with a face value of 500 yen each. Each Dai-Ichi Kangyo Investment Management share, with a face value of 50,000 yen, will be exchanged for seven Asahi shares, they said in the statement.
The combined managed assets of the three firms totalled 2.45 trillion yen as of March 31, they said.

In March, when the merger plan was first announced, the three firms said the merger was aimed at providing better asset management services to both individual and corporate clients in line with Japan's planned "Big Bang" financial reforms.
Asahi Investment mainly targets individuals, while the other two firms manage assets for pension funds and other institutional investors.
